subject.title: Feature: browser upload tool fallback for non-standard file inputs (ByteUploader)

question: Should Browser upload support custom uploader targets through an explicit drop, paste, or native-drag file-injection mode, and what security contract should govern that mode?
rationale: The current implementation lacks this mode, and adding it would expand the browser file-delivery boundary beyond standard file inputs into page-controlled event handlers.

options.title: Add an explicit custom-upload mode
options.body: Define a named upload mode or separate Browser action with managed-path validation, visible semantics, docs, focused tests, and live proof against a custom uploader.

options.title: Keep upload limited to file inputs
options.body: Decline silent fallback behavior, document the limitation, and route site-specific custom uploader automation to external plugins or skills when current APIs are enough.

options.title: Defer pending live proof
options.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer or reporter supplies a redacted live ByteUploader-style reproduction showing the exact failure and target event model.

recommendation.title: Add an explicit custom-upload mode
recommendation.body: Define a named upload mode or separate Browser action with managed-path validation, visible semantics, docs, focused tests, and live proof against a custom uploader.

likelyOwner.reason: The Browser plugin upload route and historical upload changes most consistently trace to this owner signal.
